name: What kitchen layout works best for a narrow Glendale or Burbank home?

mainEntity.name: What kitchen layout works best for a narrow Glendale or Burbank home?
mainEntity.text: What kitchen layout works best for a narrow Glendale or Burbank home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Narrow kitchens in Glendale, Burbank, and similar Los Angeles neighborhoods usually perform best with layouts that preserve walking space and keep the work triangle efficient. A galley layout is often the most practical because it uses two parallel runs of cabinetry and keeps everything within reach. A compact L-shape can also work if one wall is short and the room needs a little more openness. If space is very limited, a single-wall kitchen with a separate island or peninsula elsewhere in the home may be better than forcing a large footprint into a narrow room. The layout should be driven by traffic patterns, appliance door swing, and storage needs, not by visual trends alone. In custom design, even a few inches can change how well the kitchen functions. The best layout is the one that gives enough prep space, clear circulation, and a logical cooking sequence without making the room feel congested.
acceptedAnswer.description: For a narrow kitchen, galley, single-wall, or compact L-shaped layouts often work best because they preserve circulation while keeping prep and storage efficient. The right choice depends on doorway locations, appliance placement, and how many people use the kitchen at once.
